title: Finite-colimit transport of entrywise conjugate matrices and cokernels
statement:
Let $\mathcal B,\mathcal D$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian]. Let $H:\mathcal B\to\mathcal D$ preserve finite colimits: the image under $H$ of every colimit cocone indexed by a finite small category is a colimit cocone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix objects $X\in\mathcal B$, $Y\in\mathcal D$ and an isomorphism $e:H(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$. Write $X^r=\bigoplus_{j\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)}X$ and $Y^r=\bigoplus_{j\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)}Y$, with injections $\iota_{j,X},\iota_{j,Y}$ and projections $\pi_{j,X},\pi_{j,Y}$; the biproduct relations are $\pi_i\iota_j=\delta_{ij}$ and $\sum_j\iota_j\pi_j=1$, and rank zero means the zero object.
Then $H$ preserves zero morphisms. Its finite-coproduct comparisons, followed by the coproduct of $r$ copies of $e$, give isomorphisms $E_r:H(X^r)\xrightarrow{\sim}Y^r$ satisfying
$$E_r\circ H(\iota_{j,X})=\iota_{j,Y}\circ e,\qquad \pi_{j,Y}\circ E_r=e\circ H(\pi_{j,X}),$$
also for $r=0$ with empty families of equations.
Let $m,n\geq0$, let $(p_{ij})$ be endomorphisms of $X$ and $(q_{ij})$ endomorphisms of $Y$, indexed by $i\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)$ and $j\in\operatorname{Fin}(m)$, and suppose that $e\circ H(p_{ij})=q_{ij}\circ e$ for all $i,j$. Let $p:X^m\to X^n$ and $q:Y^m\to Y^n$ be the unique maps with entries $\pi_{i,X}p\iota_{j,X}=p_{ij}$ and $\pi_{i,Y}q\iota_{j,Y}=q_{ij}$. Then
$$E_n\circ H(p)=q\circ E_m.$$
A cokernel projection $\kappa_p:X^n\to\operatorname{coker}(p)$ means $\kappa_pp=0$ and unique factorization of every map killing $p$; use the analogous projection $\kappa_q$. The displayed square induces a unique isomorphism $u:H(\operatorname{coker}(p))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{coker}(q)$ satisfying
$$u\circ H(\kappa_p)=\kappa_q\circ E_n.$$
Its inverse $v$ satisfies $v\circ\kappa_q=H(\kappa_p)\circ E_n^{-1}$. No faithfulness, exactness, preservation of infinite colimits, or nonzero-rank assumption on $H,X,Y,m,n$ is required.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-preserving-colimits-additive], $H$ is additive: its hypotheses are exactly our abelian categories and preservation of finite colimits. In each abelian group of morphisms, $H(0)=H(0+0)=H(0)+H(0)$ implies $H(0)=0$ by cancellation. Thus all zero morphisms, including those involving rank zero, are preserved.

For every $r\geq0$, $X^r$ with its injections is the colimit of the finite discrete diagram on $r$ copies of $X$. Hence $(H(X^r),(H(\iota_{j,X})))$ is a coproduct of $r$ copies of $H(X)$, by the hypothesis on $H$ and [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Also $(Y^r,(\iota_{j,Y}e))$ is a coproduct of the same diagram: a family $a_j:H(X)\to T$ corresponds to $(a_je^{-1}:Y\to T)$. The unique isomorphism between these colimit cocones is $E_r$, and $E_rH(\iota_{j,X})=\iota_{j,Y}e$. This is exactly the finite-coproduct comparison followed by the coproduct of the copies of $e$, since that composite has these same restrictions. For $r=0$ both cocones are initial, and colimit uniqueness gives the same isomorphism.

proof.text: To prove the projection equation for fixed $i<r$, compare the maps $\pi_{i,Y}E_r$ and $eH(\pi_{i,X})$ out of the coproduct $H(X^r)$. On $H(\iota_{j,X})$ their values are $\pi_{i,Y}\iota_{j,Y}e$ and $eH(\pi_{i,X}\iota_{j,X})$. Both are $e$ when $i=j$ and zero otherwise, using the biproduct relations and step 1. Coproduct uniqueness therefore gives $\pi_{i,Y}E_r=eH(\pi_{i,X})$. If $r=0$ there is no $i$ to check.

proof.text: For clarity, arbitrary entries really determine maps, including empty matrices. Set $p=\sum_{i<n,j<m}\iota_{i,X}p_{ij}\pi_{j,X}$ and analogously $q=\sum_{i<n,j<m}\iota_{i,Y}q_{ij}\pi_{j,Y}$. Distributivity and $\pi_i\iota_j=\delta_{ij}$ give the specified entries. For any map $t:X^m\to X^n$, inserting the two identities $1=\sum_i\iota_i\pi_i$ and $1=\sum_j\iota_j\pi_j$ gives $t=\sum_{i,j}\iota_i(\pi_it\iota_j)\pi_j$. Thus the entries determine the map uniquely. These finite sums and distributivity belong to the preadditive structure of [def-sp-abelian]. Empty sums are zero, and the rank-zero identity is $1_0=0$, so the same calculation covers $m=0$ or $n=0$.

proof.text: Let $a=E_nH(p)$ and $b=qE_m$, both maps $H(X^m)\to Y^n$. For every $i<n,j<m$, steps 2 and 3 and functoriality give $\pi_{i,Y}aH(\iota_{j,X})=eH(\pi_{i,X}p\iota_{j,X})=eH(p_{ij})=q_{ij}e=\pi_{i,Y}q\iota_{j,Y}e=\pi_{i,Y}bH(\iota_{j,X})$. The target projections detect equality: if all $\pi_i s=\pi_i t$, then $s=(\sum_i\iota_i\pi_i)s=(\sum_i\iota_i\pi_i)t=t$. Hence $aH(\iota_{j,X})=bH(\iota_{j,X})$ for every $j$; the source coproduct universal property now yields $a=b$. This also handles empty families: for $n=0$ the target identity is zero, and for $m=0$ the source is initial.

proof.text: Write $K_p=\operatorname{coker}(p)$, $K_q=\operatorname{coker}(q)$ and $k=H(\kappa_p)$. The cokernel universal property in the statement is precisely the coequalizer property for the two arrows $p,0:X^m\rightrightarrows X^n$: a map $t$ coequalizes them exactly when $tp=0$. More explicitly, a cocone also has a leg from $X^m$, forced to be $tp=t0=0$, so that it is completely specified by this $t$. The parallel-pair indexing category has two objects and just two nonidentity arrows, hence is finite and small. Preservation of this colimit, together with $H(0)=0$, shows that $k$ is a cokernel of $H(p)$. In particular $kH(p)=H(\kappa_pp)=0$, and any $t:H(X^n)\to T$ killing $H(p)$ factors uniquely through $k$.

source.place: Tag 002F, definition-colimit and the immediately following uniqueness observation; finite discrete and parallel-pair diagrams

proof.text: Step 5 gives $E_nH(p)=qE_m$. Therefore $(\kappa_qE_n)H(p)=\kappa_qqE_m=0$. The cokernel property of $k$ from step 6 gives a unique map $u:H(K_p)\to K_q$ with $uk=\kappa_qE_n$. Multiplying the square by the inverses of $E_n,E_m$ gives $E_n^{-1}q=H(p)E_m^{-1}$, so $(kE_n^{-1})q=kH(p)E_m^{-1}=0$. The defining cokernel property of $\kappa_q$ gives a unique $v:K_q\to H(K_p)$ with $v\kappa_q=kE_n^{-1}$. These constructions use the cokernel universal properties already present in the statement; no existence or preservation theorem is being assumed.

source.place: Constructible complexes, via the local coefficient models on strata: categorical finite-coproduct, entrywise matrix, and cokernel arguments abstracted from the scalar presentation

proof.text: Using step 7, $(vu)k=v\kappa_qE_n=kE_n^{-1}E_n=k$ and $(uv)\kappa_q=ukE_n^{-1}=\kappa_qE_nE_n^{-1}=\kappa_q$. Uniqueness in the two cokernel universal properties gives $vu=1_{H(K_p)}$ and $uv=1_{K_q}$. Thus $u$ is an isomorphism with inverse $v$, and both required projection equations hold. Any other isomorphism with the stated equation has the same underlying morphism by uniqueness of factorization through $k$, so $u$ is unique. All constructions used only finite discrete diagrams, the finite parallel-pair diagram, biproduct identities, and the hypotheses in the statement; the proof covers either zero rank and the zero functor.
